lines.text: Every setting, rule, skill and agent in your coding setup lives at a scope.
The scope decides who it applies to:|just you, everyone on the project, or your whole organization.
Claude Code has four settings scopes.
User settings, in your home .claude folder, follow you into every project.
lines.say: User settings, in your home dot claude folder, follow you into every project.

lines.text: Shared project settings are committed to the repository,|so the whole team gets them.
Project local settings are yours alone, in one project.
When two disagree, the more specific scope wins,|and managed settings from your organization override them all.
The same split runs through every layer.
Rules: a CLAUDE.md for you, one for the project,|and a local one that stays on your machine.
lines.say: Rules: a Claude dot M D for you, one for the project, and a local one that stays on your machine.

lines.text: Skills and agents: a folder in .claude, at home or in the project.
lines.say: Skills and agents: a folder in dot claude, at home or in the project.

lines.text: MCP servers: your user config, or a .mcp.json the team commits.
lines.say: M C P servers: your user config, or a dot M C P dot JSON the team commits.

lines.text: Rules files don't replace each other: they all load, broadest first.|Permission lists merge too.
Rule of thumb: if it's true in every repo, put it in user scope.|If a teammate needs it, put it in the project.
One trap: a local settings file you make by hand isn't ignored by git.|Add it to .gitignore yourself.
lines.say: One trap: a local settings file you make by hand isn't ignored by git. Add it to dot git ignore yourself.

lines.text: Codex keeps the same split, with .codex at home and in the project,|and it skips the project's folder until you trust it.
lines.say: Codex keeps the same split, with dot codex at home and in the project, and it skips the project's folder until you trust it.
